paper_claims.claim: Average return responses gamma_k are positive at every annual lag k = 12-240 (and negative at short nonannual lags): a persistent periodic annual pattern in the cross-section of stock returns.

Winner-loser decile spreads formed only on annual lag months are significantly positive for formation intervals out to 20 years (52-115 bp/month EW, t > 5), while all-months and nonannual strategies exhibit long-term reversal (-39 to -125 bp/month).

Fama-French (1993) three-factor risk adjustment does not explain the seasonal spreads: annual-strategy alphas stay positive and significant, and annual strategies have approximately zero factor loadings.

The seasonal pattern reflects a large cross-sectional variance in seasonal expected returns: sigma^2_mu = 1.33 basis points (t = 3.57) from annual-lag WRSS profits, implying a 1.15%/month cross-sectional SD, versus approximately zero for all and nonannual lags.
The seasonal effect is independent of size, industry, calendar month, earnings announcements, dividends, and fiscal year-end.

tables.description: Average return responses from monthly cross-sectional simple (Panel A) and multiple (Panel B, 3 specs) regressions at lags 1-240.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates the Fama-MacBeth regression machinery: PIT NYSE/AMEX universe 1965-2002, formation-month availability rule (stocks with returns at t and t-k only), simple regressions at lags 1-12 and each 12th through 240, the three multiple-regression specifications of Panel B, and Newey-West(12) t-statistics. Validates the paper's core discovery - the annual-lag pulse train in return responses.
tables.paper_quote: Monthly simple cross-sectional regressions of the form $r_{i,t} = \alpha_{k,t} + \gamma_{k,t} r_{i,t-k} + u_{i,t}$ are calculated for each month $t$ and lag $k$ [...] The reported Fama and MacBeth (1973) $t$ -statistics are corrected for heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation (using Newey and West, 1987, correction with 12 lags). (L180)
tables.notes: Estimates are printed in percent (L180). gamma has a portfolio-return interpretation (Eq. 2, L118-137).

tables.description: WRSS profits pi_k(t) averaged over All/Nonannual/Annual lag groups: the sigma^2_mu estimator of cross-sectional variance in seasonal expected returns.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates the weighted relative-strength-strategy computation - products of market-excess returns over all month pairs (t, t-k) on the common cross-section - grouped into All/Nonannual/Annual lags, with the paper's sqrt(500) SE convention. Validates the economic-magnitude claim (sigma^2_mu = 1.33 bp, seasonal cross-sectional SD 1.15%/month).
tables.paper_quote: For every pair of month $t$ and its lag month $k$ we calculate the return of each stock in each month excess of the equally weighed market return that month (using the cross-section of stocks with available returns in both months $j$ and $k$ ). [...] Standard errors are calculated by dividing the population standard deviation of each group by the square root of 500. (L1192)
tables.notes: pi is a product of two percent returns (percent-squared); the paper's table label is 'Mean (percent)'. Sample January 1963 - December 2002, annual lags k = 12..468 (L1192, L1231).

tables.description: 10-1 spreads in event vs nonevent months for earnings announcements (A), dividend announcements (B), ex-dividend months (C), and fiscal-year-end months (D).
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates conditioning holding months on Compustat-recorded events (earnings-announcement months, dividend-declaration months, ex-dividend months, fiscal-year-end months) with deciles re-formed within the conditioned samples (L2420). Validates that seasonality is not driven by information-release events.
tables.paper_quote: The sample in each panel includes only NYSE- and AMEX-listed firms whose respective events are recorded on Compustat. The table reports the portfolio returns using only returns during event months and only returns during nonevent months. (L2434)
tables.notes: Event dates from CRSP/Compustat: earnings announcements via Compustat report dates, dividend declarations and ex-dates via CRSP msedist, fiscal-year-end via Compustat datadate. Exact event-date fields to be verified at Stage 5.
